$comment: Every playable traveller, and where their frames come from.
This replaced two hand-written invocations in package.json with a colour count typed into
each. Two characters was tolerable; five characters across seven sheets is not, and the
sitting art is packed two and three to a file, which no command line should have to remember.
A sixth traveller is a row here and nothing else.
walk:  a 4x4 sheet, one character, sixteen frames -- four per facing, in the order
findSprites returns them (down, up, right, left).
sit:   one frame per facing. The new sitting art gives one pose per direction rather than
four, and that is enough: a seated figure has nowhere to walk to. `frames` names which
figures to take from a packed sheet, in reading order, because position-in-row is not
reliable -- see the note on --frames in build-sprite-sheet.js.
colours: per character, never shared. At 26x40 it is hue that tells one person from another,
and quantising three characters together starves all three.

characters.name: Varuna
$sit_comment: Seated right and left were built the wrong way round: frame 18 faced left and 19 right,
checked by eye at 8x beside his walking profiles. In the dugout that sat him facing the
stern. `order` carries them across swapped; there is no seated source to rebuild from.

characters.name: Guyuk
$walk_comment: Third sheet for this character, and the third different answer on row order -- which is
the reason this comment exists rather than a frame list. The original art was down, up,
right, left; the replacement was down, up, LEFT, right and needed a reorder here; this one
is back to down, up, right, left and needs none.
Row order is a property of the file in hand, never of the character. Check it by eye at
about 18x every time a sheet is replaced, and delete a stale `frames` list when the new
art no longer needs it -- carrying one forward silently re-breaks what it once fixed.

characters.name: Mithra
$walk_comment: Mithra's profile rows arrive the other way round, and only Mithra's do.
findSprites returns this sheet as down, up, LEFT, right -- so the built sheet put the
left-facing art at frames 8-11, which is where WALK_ROW in src/game/player.ts says the
right-facing art lives. Walking east played a figure facing west while it slid east: a
moonwalk, and the one every other character does not do.
Reordered here rather than in the game. The four-row convention is one every other sheet
already keeps, and one character's art should not bend it for the other four. --frames
reorders as well as selects (boxes = wanted.map(...)), so naming all sixteen in the order
the game expects is the whole fix.
Verified by eye at 18x, which is the only way this class of fault is caught: frame 10
faces left and frame 14 faces right in the source, and the pair swap under this list.

$comment: Third and last traveller sheet, and the one that completes the set -- `TRAVELLER_SHEETS`
in content/travellers.ts can only switch when it can cover a whole map, which is three.
Best gait of the three: stride 7.5/7.0 with the feet closing to zero on both profile rows,
against the carrier's 6.5/7.0 and Mithra's 5.0. The solarpunk theme is in the subject rather
than the style block -- she walks the road planting and tending what grows along it, which
is the person who makes canon's three new wayside species true. docs/art-direction.md warns
that 'solarpunk' in a style block returns solar panels and brass gauges into a 4000 BCE
setting, so the prompt carries an explicit anachronism block as well.
characters.name: A pilgrim

$comment: Second traveller sheet. Its first attempt passed every automated check and was sent back
anyway: the back view filled 34 of 40 rows because the staff was held out to the side, so
the figure shrank about 15% as it turned away -- `resample` fits each figure's own bounding
box to the cell, and a back view wider than it is tall gets fitted by width. Holding the
staff close in against the body fixed it: heights are 40,40,40,40 and widths 21-23.
The other fault was the contrast block not contrasting. The prompt asked for a white
headwrap differing from 'the clothing' without naming the clothing's colour, so the tunic
came back white too and head and torso merged into one pale mass. The tunic is dark
olive-green now and the head reads as separate.
characters.name: A drover

$comment: The first sheet that draws a traveller and nobody else. `SHEETS` in content/travellers.ts
used to be the five playable characters, so everybody met on the road wore a face the
player could also be wearing -- and on the map you were on, one of the three might be
wearing yours.
colours: 12, not the 26 Mithra takes. Measured on this exact source: 15.9% speckle at 12
against 27.4% at 18. A carried load adds colours the figure does not otherwise need, and
these are drawn at half the player's size where the count is the least visible thing about
them. `node tools/check-sprite.js` is the check.
sit: the walking source again, taking the first frame of each row. A traveller NEVER sits --
`updateTravellers` only ever plays 'walk' -- but the builder requires all twenty frames, and
four standing poses are the honest filler. Inventing a seated pose for a figure nothing ever
seats would be art nobody looks at. Replace it the day a traveller can be sat down.
No `frames` reorder: checked by eye at 9x, the rows arrive down, up, right, left.
characters.name: A carrier
